dispatched_notes: AAM mission page (390-10) gives 390BG (15). 390th Memorial Museum mission 023 synopsis (390-02): group "ordered to furnish eighteen bombers", flying with three 100th BG bombers in the same combat box (those are in 100th.json); "two hours after takeoff, the Group lost four planes" to aborts (not named). The museum personnel/mission DB (390-01) lists 16 390th aircraft / 164 crew-sorties for mission 023. Whether the 4 aborts are among the 16 (=> 12 attacking + lost) or additional to them is unresolved, so dispatched left null (16 aircraft in the museum DB vs 15 in AAM vs 18 ordered). 100th BG Foundation (390-11) says FOUR 100th crews flew with the 390th (museum: three) - those are in 100th.json. Lost = 1 (42-29991, MACR 858).

aircraft.notes: 390th Museum DB (390-01) lists this aircraft as 'Unknown', crew number 29. Nickname = aircraft name(s) in the museum DB across the airframe's career ('/' separates successive/alternate names); not confirmed as painted on 14 Oct 1943. Squadron 568th per b17flyingfortress.de squadron list (390-04) and American Air Museum assignment record (390-08, codes BI-N); these are the airframe's assignment, not a 14 Oct 1943 document - code letters PROBABLE for this date. Outcome unknown: the museum narrative (390-02) says four 390th aircraft aborted about two hours after take-off for mechanical problems or crew illness, but does not name them; this sortie may be one of them, or may have bombed. CONFLICT: 390-01 (museum mission DB) places the Rowland crew in 42-3526 on 14 Oct 1943. AAM (390-08) says 42-3526 was "abandoned during assembly for Schweinfurt 14/10/43 with Bob Sabel (inj), Co-pilot: John Wenzel (inj)" and crashed at Knockbridge Farm, Icklesham, near Hastings, salvaged 20/10/43 (b17flyingfortress.de loss list 390-09 also has "Crashed on take off" on 14 Oct 1943). But 390-01 has John E. Wenzel flying as co-pilot to Geary in 42-30325 to the target that day, and other AAM person pages give the bail-out as 18 Oct 1943 (recalled mission, engine fire). The Sabel incident is therefore probably 18 Oct 1943, not this mission (unresolved). Outcome for the Rowland sortie left unknown. AAM notes Rowland was a 570th BS pilot.

aircraft.loss_details: Hit by flak over the target (No. 3 engine, also reports of Nos. 1 and 2 hit), then 20mm fire from a single fighter split a wing fuel tank; left formation near the rally point (~1500-1523 hrs) with two/three engines feathered, ~23,000 ft; witnesses saw 8-10 parachutes. Crashed at Lohrweg near Gondelsheim, ~9 miles E of Karlsruhe (eyewitnesses place the action ~20 miles NE of Karlsruhe). Claimed by Uffz. Hermann Bolten (unit given in source as "KG 2./11", sic), flying an Me 410A-1. All 10 crew POW.

research_gaps: Which four 390th aircraft aborted is not identified; outcome left "unknown" for 11 aircraft whose crews do not appear in the MACR 858 eyewitness list. Next step: 390th mission report file no. 987-988 (Mission Reports Part I, 390th Memorial Museum Joseph A. Moller Library) or the 390th loading list.

Ranks on 14 Oct 1943 not found for most crew; the 390th DB mission listing gives no ranks. Individual personnel records (390-01, Personnel Search) were not opened one-by-one. Ranks recorded only for the McEwin crew (390-03) and MACR 858 eyewitnesses.

Squadron and code letters per aircraft are the airframe assignment from b17flyingfortress.de and AAM/Osborne (390-04..08), not from a 14 Oct 1943 loading list; 42-30642 moved 568th (BI-O) to 569th (CC-O) at an undocumented date.
Formation positions not documented in sources seen (Jeffrey/Clark command crew in 42-30338 and Tuttle as command pilot in 42-3327 indicate lead/deputy-lead roles, unconfirmed).
Battle damage/wounded on returning aircraft not documented in sources seen (museum synopsis notes many damaged by flak and one with friendly .50 cal hits, unnamed).
No service numbers recorded (not seen in the sources used).
